title: Dimension bound for a finite type Laurent polynomial subalgebra
statement: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with finite Krull dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $L=R[t,t^{-1}]$ denote the ring of finite sums $\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}r_it^i$, with $r_i\in R$, coefficientwise addition and convolution multiplication. Let $B\subseteq L$ be an $R$-subalgebra containing the constant copy of $R$, and assume $B$ is of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Then $\dim B\leq d+1$. No reducedness, domain, locality or catenarity hypothesis on $R$ or $B$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0BAG (lemma-alteration-dimension-general), with Tag 0BAE (lemma-dimension-formula-general): algebraic consequence for finite type subalgebras of a one-variable Laurent polynomial algebra, including the reduction along minimal primes.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes], enumerate the minimal primes of $R$ as $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_s$. This family is nonempty: otherwise [lem-per-nilradical-minimal-prime-intersection] would make $1$ nilpotent in the nonzero ring $R$. Put $D_i=R/\mathfrak p_i$ and $F_i=\operatorname{Frac}(D_i)$; these are a domain and its fraction field [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra]. Coefficient reduction gives a ring map $\rho_i:B\to D_i[t,t^{-1}]\subset F_i(t)$, where the last field is [def-weil-rational-function-field]. Addition and multiplication commute with reduction because their coefficients are finite sums of coefficients and products. The last inclusion is injective: multiplying a finite Laurent sum by a large power of $t$ gives a polynomial, whose coefficients vanish if its image in $F_i(t)$ vanishes. Let $K_i=\ker\rho_i$. Since the target is a field and $\rho_i(1)=1$, $K_i$ is prime; its contraction to $R$ is $\mathfrak p_i$, by testing constant coefficients.

source.place: Tag 0BAG (lemma-alteration-dimension-general), applied after the explicit coefficient/minimal-prime reduction; Tag 0BAE (lemma-dimension-formula-general).

proof.text: If $b\in\bigcap_iK_i$, every Laurent coefficient $r_j$ of $b$ belongs to all $\mathfrak p_i$, hence is nilpotent by [lem-per-nilradical-minimal-prime-intersection]. For its finitely many nonzero coefficients choose $e_j\geq1$ with $r_j^{e_j}=0$. In any product of $M=1+\sum_j(e_j-1)$ coefficients, one $r_j$ occurs at least $e_j$ times, so each monomial in the expansion of $b^M$ vanishes. Thus $b$ is nilpotent (if $b$ has no nonzero coefficient, then $b=0$ and $M=1$). Since a nilpotent element lies in every prime ideal of $B$, every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ contains $\bigcap_iK_i$, and hence contains some $K_i$: otherwise choose $b_i\in K_i\setminus\mathfrak q$; then $\prod_i b_i\in\bigcap_iK_i\subseteq\mathfrak q$, contradicting primality. Consequently every minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ equals some $K_i$, since $K_i$ is itself prime.

source.place: Tag 0BAG (lemma-alteration-dimension-general), applied after the explicit coefficient/minimal-prime reduction; Tag 0BAE (lemma-dimension-formula-general).

proof.text: Fix a minimal prime $\mathfrak q=K_i$ of $B$ and write $E=\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)$. The map $B/\mathfrak q\hookrightarrow F_i(t)$ extends to an embedding $E\hookrightarrow F_i(t)$ by $a/b\mapsto\rho_i(a)/\rho_i(b)$. Denominators are nonzero; the fraction equality $ab\prime=a\prime b$ verifies well-definedness, and a fraction maps to zero only if its numerator is zero. The constants give an injection $D_i\hookrightarrow B/\mathfrak q$, since $K_i\cap R=\mathfrak p_i$. Thus $F_i\hookrightarrow E$ by the same fraction formula, and the composite into $F_i(t)$ is its usual constant embedding. In particular all embeddings commute with $R\to R/\mathfrak p_i$; this is the residue-field extension $\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)$, not a fibre ring.

source.place: Tag 0BAG (lemma-alteration-dimension-general), applied after the explicit coefficient/minimal-prime reduction; Tag 0BAE (lemma-dimension-formula-general).

proof.text: Every $z\in F_i(t)$ has a presentation $P(t)/Q(t)$ with $Q\ne0$ [def-weil-rational-function-field]. It satisfies the nonzero polynomial $Q(t)Z-P(t)$ over the subalgebra $F_i[t]$: its coefficient of $Z$ is nonzero. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-adjoin-transcendence-bound] with base $F_i$, domain algebra $F_i(t)$ and singleton $\{t\}$ to get $\operatorname{trdeg}_{F_i}F_i(t)\leq1$. Any algebraically independent subset of $E$ stays algebraically independent in $F_i(t)$: a polynomial relation there is zero in $E$ by injectivity of step 3, with the same constant coefficients. The definition [def-kun-transcendence-degree] therefore gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_{F_i}E\leq1$.

source.place: Tag 030F (lemma-transcendence-degree), proof: a generating set contains a transcendence basis; algebraic-adjoin cardinal bound, specialized to the rational-function field generated by one indeterminate.

proof.text: Form $f:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Its source and target are the affine pair in [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion], so finite type of $B$ over $R$ gives local finite type of $f$. The one-member affine covering of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ gives local Noetherianity by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] and the closure formula [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], the generic points of its source components are precisely the minimal primes $\mathfrak q$ of $B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field], their residue fields are $\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)$ and those of their images are $\operatorname{Frac}(R/(\mathfrak q\cap R))$. The residue-field map is the fraction map induced by $R\to B$, by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-residue-field-naturality]. Thus step 4 gives the exact generic residue-field bound $1$ required by Tag 0BAG.

source.place: Tag 0BAG (lemma-alteration-dimension-general), applied after the explicit coefficient/minimal-prime reduction; Tag 0BAE (lemma-dimension-formula-general).

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], topological dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ equals $\dim R=d$, and likewise that of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ equals $\dim B$. Apply [lem-sfb-generic-residue-transcendence-dimension-bound] to $f$ with $n=1$: step 5 verifies local finite type, local Noetherianity of the base and the bound at every generic point. It yields $\dim B=\dim\operatorname{Spec}B\leq\dim\operatorname{Spec}R+1=d+1$.
